extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, GME program directors, Medicare administrative contractors (MACs), and health policy/regulatory staff implementing Medicare GME/IME/DGME rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for determining whether a medical residency program is 'new' for Medicare cap-building purposes and related DGME/IME payment calculations following hospital mergers. Includes definitional rules, counting methods, exceptions, reporting instructions, and post-merger payment methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a new medical residency training program
rubrics_metrics.description: A new medical residency training program means a program that receives initial accreditation by the appropriate accrediting body or begins training residents on or after January 1, 1995, and that meets the conditions specified (including, subject to provisions, the 90 percent new resident requirement effective for programs started on or after October 1, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text proposed to revise 42 CFR 413.79(l) to reflect this definition and the associated conditions. Effective for programs starting on or after October 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of initial accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial accreditation from the appropriate accrediting body is a required element for newness but CMS will not rely solely on accrediting body characterization to determine whether a program is genuinely new for cap-building purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS retains concern about inappropriate duplication or relocation of FTE cap slots; therefore, accreditation alone is insufficient — other factors (notably the resident newness threshold) are applied to prevent transfers of existing programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of restriction based on previous employment of faculty and program directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective for programs started on or after October 1, 2026, CMS would no longer consider the previous employment of the faculty or program director in determining whether a residency program should be considered genuinely new for cap-building purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs started earlier but still within five-year cap-building period as of October 1, 2026, remain subject to the August 27, 2009 newness criteria. CMS concluded that prior employment of faculty/program directors is an overly restrictive supporting factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90 percent new resident threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to receiving initial accreditation, at least 90 percent of the individual resident trainees (not FTEs) entering the program during the five-year cap-building period must not have previous training in the same specialty as the new program for the program to be considered new (effective for programs started on or after October 1, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 90 percent threshold operationalizes the concept of an 'overwhelming majority.' The threshold is applied to individual trainees (counted as persons), not weighted FTEs. Precedent exists in section 5506 regulations where 90% denotes 'entire' program takeover. The proposal excludes certain categories (see separate exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting method across the five-year cap-building period
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the 90 percent threshold is determined by tallying all individual residents who enter the program during the five-year cap-building period (first five program years for new urban teaching hospitals or first five program years of each new program for rural hospitals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If 50 trainees enter over five years, at least 45 (90% of 50) must be new first-year residents in that specialty. Standard rounding: round down when remainder < 0.5, round up when remainder >= 0.5 (e.g., 90% of 48 = 43.2 rounds down to 43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding rules for numerical threshold calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply standard rounding when the quotient is not a whole number: round down when remainder < 0.5; round up when remainder >= 0.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to convert fractional required counts into whole-person thresholds for the 90 percent requirement. Example given: 90% of 48 = 43.2 => 43 required new residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAC review timing for newness determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) will review the previous training experience of each individual trainee and determine program newness prior to calculating IME and DGME cap adjustments at the end of the five-year cap-building period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with historical policy, the MAC is not required to provide an initial assessment of newness prior to the end of the cap-building period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for residents admitted via binding matching programs (e.g., NRMP Match)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals with previous experience training in another program in the same specialty who enter the new program as first-year residents through the National Resident Matching Program or another binding third-party resident matching program are excluded from both the numerator and denominator when determining compliance with the 90 percent requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS recognizes hospitals cannot predict final Match outcomes and should not be penalized. Those excluded individuals are nonetheless reported on the new resident lines of the hospital cost report and included in the calculation of the hospital's permanent cap adjustment at the conclusion of the cap-building period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion and reporting of displaced residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Residents who meet the definition of a 'displaced resident' under 42 CFR 413.79(h)(1)(iii) are excluded from both the numerator and denominator of the 90 percent calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displaced residents must not be reported on the new resident lines or included in permanent cap adjustments; instead they are reported on displaced resident lines (lines 16 and 16.01 of Worksheet E-4 and line 17 of Worksheet E, Part A) if the hospital qualifies for a temporary cap adjustment under 42 CFR 413.79(h). Otherwise they are reported on regular FTE lines, subject to existing caps. Rotation schedules (not cost report entries) are used to identify individual residents for the permanent cap calculation; displaced residents listed on rotation schedules are excluded from new program cap calculation. Hospitals training displaced residents may receive priority for cap slots under section 5506 if they apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting treatment during cap-building period for excluded categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Although excluded from the 90 percent count, certain excluded individuals (e.g., first-year residents admitted via Match) are reported on new program lines during the cap-building period and later included/excluded appropriately in the permanent cap calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If 50 trainees include 4 Match-admitted previously-trained individuals and 2 displaced residents, the 4 Match individuals would be excluded from the 90% calculation but still reported on new program lines; the 2 displaced residents would be reported on displaced or regular lines and excluded from the newness count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small program exception (<=16 positions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'small' residency program, defined as one accredited for 16 or fewer resident (or fellow) positions, is exempt from the 90 percent new resident requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small programs must still obtain initial accreditation but are not required to achieve any minimum proportion of new residents to be considered new for cap-building purposes. The definition applies regardless of urban/rural designation (i.e., geographic designation does not affect the <=16 rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on commingling of residents
rubrics_metrics.description: No distinct restrictions proposed on commingling; program newness is determined by initial accreditation and the 90 percent new resident threshold regardless of whether residents share educational experiences with an existing program in the same specialty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will consider a program new for cap-building purposes if it has initial accreditation and meets the 90% threshold (with exceptions), even if clinical/didactic experiences are shared across programs — consistent with ACGME practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on multiple programs in the same specialty at one hospital
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital may operate two or more programs in the same specialty for cap-building purposes if each additional program has separate initial accreditation and at least 90 percent new individual trainees entering during the five-year cap-building period (subject to exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a change from prior policy (which allowed multiple programs provided they had separate directors/staff/separately matched residents without additional requirements). The 90% new resident criterion (except for small programs and other exclusions) now applies to subsequently accredited programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date application
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed policies (including removal of faculty employment restriction and the 90% new resident threshold and exceptions) would be effective for programs starting on or after October 1, 2026; programs started earlier but still within their five-year cap-building period remain subject to prior criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory changes are tied to program start dates; hospitals must track program start dates to know which standard applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: DGME payment calculation following hospital mergers — pre/post merger separation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a merger involves teaching hospitals, DGME payment for a surviving hospital's cost reporting period that includes the merger must be calculated by treating the pre-merger and post-merger portions as two short cost reporting periods with distinct payment rates and inputs, then summing the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the surviving hospital begins a new cost reporting period effective with the merger date, payments are determined based on new combined DGME payment rates. If merger occurs mid-period, MAC performs off-the-cost-report calculations treating timeframes as if they were two short cost reporting periods; pre-merger uses surviving provider data alone; post-merger uses merged data and updated PRAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTE resident count calculation for partial-year pre/post-merger periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial-year unweighted DGME FTE counts are calculated by summing allowable rotations for all residents during each period and dividing by 365 or 366 using rotation schedules or similar sources; weighted counts apply specialty weighting factors and are determined separately for primary care and non-primary care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-merger counts include rotations allowable to the surviving provider only; post-merger counts include the sum of allowable rotations for the merged entity. See August 4, 2025 FR guidance (90 FR 36915-16) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTE resident limit (cap) proration for pre/post-merger periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial-year DGME FTE resident limits are calculated by prorating hospitals' original full-year FTE caps (including adjustments) for the number of days in each respective pre- and post-merger period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-merger limit derived from surviving provider's FTE caps only; post-merger limit includes combined caps of all merged hospitals. If merged hospitals have rural track or section 422 counts, those are determined and applied separately. Applies standard proration methods (see 90 FR 36917).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rolling average FTE count and virtual rolling average after merger
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-year rolling average inputs (current, prior, penultimate weighted FTE counts) must be determined separately for pre- and post-merger periods; a 'virtual' rolling average combining surviving and terminating providers' counts must be created for the merged provider's first two cost reporting periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current-year counts computed as explained; prior and penultimate counts obtained from lines 12 and 13 of Worksheet E-4 of respective hospitals' cost reports and prorated. The virtual rolling average simulates the merger during the prior/penultimate years (prorating as necessary). Standard rolling average computation resumes in the third full post-merger cost reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per resident amount determination pre- and post-merger
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-merger DGME payment uses the surviving provider's PRAs updated to the midpoint of the pre-merger period; post-merger payment uses merged PRA(s) determined per prior rulemaking and updated to the midpoint of the post-merger period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merged PRA(s) are calculated according to August 18, 2006 policy (71 FR 48075-6) and updated for inflation (e.g., CPI-U) to appropriate midpoints. If Section 422 special per resident amounts apply, they are calculated separately for each period and updated similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare patient load calculation pre/post merger (Part A and MA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate Medicare Part A and Medicare Advantage patient loads are determined for pre- and post-merger periods using Provider Statistical and Reimbursement (PS&R) report data: pre-merger uses surviving provider inpatient days; post-merger uses the sum of inpatient days for all merged hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a pre- or post-merger period straddles January 1, separate MA patient loads must be determined for portions before and after Jan 1 to apply different calendar-year MA DGME percentage reductions (per § 413.76(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-the-cost-report calculations and cost report placeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the cost report cannot support multiple DGME payment rates for portions of a single cost year, MACs perform the pre- and post-merger calculations off the cost report and sum the results; placeholder values based on combined rates are reported as necessary on Worksheet E-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sum of off-the-cost-report DGME payments is reported on line 31 of Worksheet E-4. Terminating hospitals file terminating cost reports for their pre-merger periods and receive DGME payments per short cost reporting period rules.
